message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – Key Properties

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotopes** | ^1H (protium), ^2H (deuterium), ^3H (tritium) |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average weighted by natural abundance) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ/mol) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (0.00008988 g/cm³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Bond type** | Covalent (in H₂ molecules) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water or oxides depending on conditions |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺ in solution) or base (forming H⁻ in hydride compounds) |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant, laboratory standard gas, semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). |

**Chemical behavior highlights**

* Forms diatomic molecules (H₂) under normal conditions.
* In aqueous solution, it behaves as a proton donor (acidic) forming H₃O⁺.
* In metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), it behaves as a hydride ion (H⁻).
* Combines with oxygen to form water (exothermic reaction).

These values give a quick snapshot of hydrogen’s fundamental characteristics.
